# Purpose

This tutorial demonstrates the full `bottom-UpR` workflow on reproducible
synthetic data. The synthetic generator is intended for teaching and software
testing. It does not reproduce the data-generating process of Cameroon or any
other specific country.

# 1. Simulate enumeration-area data

```r
library(bottom.UpR)
library(INLA)

# Full-data simulation.
ea_full <- simulate_bottom_up_data(
  n = 250,
  seed = 2026,
  include_hierarchy = TRUE,
  chunkwise = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Chunk-wise simulation with the same seed.
ea_chunked <- simulate_bottom_up_data(
  n = 250,
  seed = 2026,
  include_hierarchy = TRUE,
  chunkwise = TRUE,
  chunk_size = 60,
  verbose = TRUE
)

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      ea_full,
      ea_chunked,
      tolerance = 0,
      check.attributes = TRUE
    )
  )
)

ea <- ea_full

head(ea)
```

The data contain mapped building counts, projected coordinates, five continuous
covariates, PPB and count responses, and optional source/settlement/region/EA
grouping variables. With the same seed, full-data and chunk-wise simulation use
the same random-number stream and return the same synthetic data.

The complete package warning catalogue can be inspected with:

```r
warnings <- bottom_up_warning_catalogue()
warnings
```

A runnable warning demonstration is installed at
`inst/examples/synthetic_warning_demo.R`. It intentionally triggers
deterministic warning conditions and prints the remaining diagnostic warnings
that cannot be forced safely in a tutorial.

```r
candidate_covariates <- c(
  "roads", "water", "market", "slope", "night_lights"
)
```

# 2. Explore the data

```r
plot_bottom_up_exploration(
  ea,
  response = "population_count",
  buildings = "buildings",
  covariates = candidate_covariates
)

plot_bottom_up_exploration(
  ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  covariates = candidate_covariates
)
```

# 3. Define an optional hierarchy

```r
effects <- list(
  list(column = "source", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "settlement", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "region_settlement", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "ea_id", model = "iid", prediction = "known")
)
```

All effects are optional. A simpler model can use
`hierarchical_effects = NULL`.

# 4. Build the SPDE mesh

```r
mesh_par <- bottom_up_mesh_parameters(
  ea,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m")
)

mesh_par$max_edge
mesh_par$offset
mesh_par$cutoff

mesh <- make_bottom_up_mesh(
  ea,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  adaptive = TRUE
)
```

# 5. Fit Gamma PPB and Negative-Binomial count models

```r
gamma_fit <- bottom_up(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  mesh = mesh,
  prior_range = c(100000, 0.05),
  prior_sigma = c(1, 0.05),
  config = TRUE
)

nb_fit <- bottom_up(
  data = ea,
  response = "population_count",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "count",
  likelihood = "negative binomial",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  mesh = mesh,
  prior_range = c(100000, 0.05),
  prior_sigma = c(1, 0.05),
  config = TRUE
)
```

For PPB models, predicted PPB is multiplied by mapped buildings when population
is requested. For count models, buildings already enter through the log
exposure and must not be multiplied again.

# 6. Automatic likelihood selection

```r
ppb_auto <- bottom_up(
  ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "auto",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  mesh = mesh
)

ppb_auto$selection$scores

count_auto <- bottom_up(
  ea,
  response = "population_count",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "count",
  likelihood = "auto",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  mesh = mesh
)

count_auto$selection$scores
```

PPB compares Gamma with Lognormal; COUNT compares Poisson with Negative
Binomial. The current default ranks compatible candidates by mean log CPO.

# 7. Observation-level posterior predictions

```r
gamma_obs <- observation_predictions(
  gamma_fit,
  draws = 300,
  seed = 11
)

head(gamma_obs)

plot_observed_fitted(gamma_fit, draws = 300)
plot_bottom_up_residuals(gamma_fit, draws = 300)
plot_posterior_fixed(gamma_fit)
plot_posterior_hyperparameters(gamma_fit)
plot_hierarchical_effects(gamma_fit, effect = "source")
plot_spatial_field(gamma_fit)
```

# 8. Spatial cross-validation with fold-specific selection

```r
selector_args <- list(
  fallback = 3,
  prior_range = c(100000, 0.05),
  prior_sigma = c(1, 0.05)
)

cv100 <- bottom_up_cv(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  method = "spatial_block",
  folds = 5,
  block_size = 100000,
  covariate_selector = bottom_up_inla_selector,
  selector_args = selector_args,
  standardize = TRUE,
  prediction_draws = 100,
  mesh = mesh,
  seed = 102
)

cv100$metrics
cv100$metrics_by_fold
cv100$selected_covariates

plot_observed_fitted(cv100)
plot_cv_diagnostics(cv100)

bottom_up_residual_moran(
  cv100,
  distances = c(50000, 100000, 150000)
)
```

Scaling and covariate selection are estimated from each training fold only.

# 10. Build a synthetic fine prediction grid

```r
grid <- expand.grid(
  x_m = seq(5000, 295000, length.out = 45),
  y_m = seq(5000, 295000, length.out = 45)
)

set.seed(303)
n <- nrow(grid)

grid$roads <- rnorm(n)
grid$water <- rnorm(n)
grid$market <- rnorm(n)
grid$slope <- rnorm(n)
grid$night_lights <- rnorm(n)

grid$buildings <- rpois(
  n,
  lambda = exp(2 + 0.15 * grid$roads - 0.08 * grid$slope)
)

grid$settlement <- sample(
  c("urban", "periurban", "rural"),
  n, replace = TRUE
)

grid$region <- sample(
  paste0("R", 1:5),
  n, replace = TRUE
)

grid$region_settlement <- interaction(
  grid$region,
  grid$settlement,
  drop = TRUE
)

grid$national <- "Syntheticland"
```

# 11. Joint-posterior fine-grid prediction

```r
gamma_grid_full <- predict_bottom_up(
  gamma_fit,
  newdata = grid,
  population = TRUE,
  draws = 250,
  chunkwise = FALSE,
  return_draws = FALSE,
  aggregate_by = c("national", "region"),
  omit_effects = "source",
  marginalize_effects = "ea_id",
  seed = 401
)

gamma_grid_chunked <- predict_bottom_up(
  gamma_fit,
  newdata = grid,
  population = TRUE,
  draws = 250,
  chunkwise = TRUE,
  chunk_size = 500,
  return_draws = FALSE,
  aggregate_by = c("national", "region"),
  omit_effects = "source",
  marginalize_effects = "ea_id",
  seed = 401
)

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    gamma_grid_full$summary,
    gamma_grid_chunked$summary,
    tolerance = 1e-10
  )),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    gamma_grid_full$aggregates$national,
    gamma_grid_chunked$aggregates$national,
    tolerance = 1e-10
  ))
)

gamma_grid <- gamma_grid_chunked

head(gamma_grid$summary)
gamma_grid$aggregates$national
gamma_grid$aggregates$region
```

The same joint posterior sample identities are retained across chunks. The
example above explicitly verifies that single-block and chunk-wise prediction
return the same posterior summaries when the same seed is used. Administrative
uncertainty is therefore computed from coherent draw-wise totals.

# 12. Count-model grid prediction

```r
nb_grid <- predict_bottom_up(
  nb_fit,
  newdata = grid,
  population = TRUE,
  draws = 250,
  chunkwise = TRUE,
  chunk_size = 500,
  aggregate_by = c("national", "region"),
  omit_effects = "source",
  marginalize_effects = "ea_id",
  seed = 402
)

nb_grid$aggregates$national
```

# 13. Structural-zero check

```r
zero_cells <- which(grid$buildings == 0)

if (length(zero_cells)) {
  stopifnot(all(gamma_grid$summary$mean[zero_cells] == 0))
  stopifnot(all(nb_grid$summary$mean[zero_cells] == 0))
}
```

# 14. Full executable script

The repository also contains a single executable script:

`inst/examples/synthetic_tutorial.R`

It runs all tutorial stages, writes tables and figures, and saves fitted models
and fine-grid posterior summaries.


# 15. Warning catalogue and runnable warning examples

List all package-level warning messages/patterns:

```r
warning_catalogue <- bottom_up_warning_catalogue()

warning_catalogue[
  c(
    "category",
    "message",
    "trigger",
    "suggested_action"
  )
]
```

Run the dedicated warning demonstration:

```r
warning_demo <- system.file(
  "examples",
  "synthetic_warning_demo.R",
  package = "bottom.UpR"
)

source(warning_demo)
```

The script intentionally demonstrates warnings for small simulations, ineffective
chunk sizes, response-type overrides, missing inputs, sparse hierarchy levels,
longitude/latitude-like coordinates, unusual mesh settings, incomplete
aggregation groups, non-finite posterior draws, Moran distance bands with no
links, and—when INLA is installed—prediction exposure/chunk warnings.

Warnings that arise only from pathological or data-dependent INLA fits (for
example CPO failures or non-zero optimization status) are catalogued but are
not deliberately manufactured.


## Faster separated cross-validation

The computationally efficient workflow separates covariate selection from
cross-validation. This avoids fitting a selector model inside every fold.

```r
selected <- bottom_up_inla_selector(
  train_data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  candidate_covariates = candidate_covariates,
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  spatial = FALSE,
  fallback = 3
)

cv_fast_workflow <- bottom_up_cv(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  fixed_covariates = selected,
  selection_mode = "separate",
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  spatial = TRUE,
  method = "spatial_block",
  folds = 5,
  block_size = 100000,
  prediction_draws = 100,
  mesh = mesh
)
```

This requires one separate selector fit followed by one fitted model per CV
fold. It does not re-fit the selector inside each fold and it reuses the common
mesh.

If the target of validation includes the selection procedure itself, use the
more expensive nested option explicitly:

```r
cv_nested <- bottom_up_cv(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  spatial = TRUE,
  method = "spatial_block",
  folds = 5,
  block_size = 100000,
  covariate_selector = bottom_up_inla_selector,
  selection_mode = "fold",
  selector_spatial = FALSE,
  selector_args = list(fallback = 3),
  prediction_draws = 100,
  mesh = mesh
)
```

The nested option is statistically stricter for evaluating the selection
procedure, but substantially more computationally expensive.
